Author: @blackforestwaltz
Content:
I get *why* they have the quarantine section set up like they do for the game, but it’s also driving me nuts.  Ah yes, let’s put all the possibly healthy people with possibly sick people!  All in a single chamber with no barriers or guards!

Edit: yes, I understand the possible reasons WHY the dev made it a single, tiny chamber (literally the first thing I said).  It’s a demo, limitations of the dev’s own time/resources, game mechanics, in-game resources/lore, etc.  What I was trying to express was that a quarantine setup like this wouldn’t work (in a zombie apocalypse or irl) and it was bugging me because it’s a stupid thing to do when you’re trying to keep as many people as possible healthy (in a zombie apocalypse or irl).
Since I’m already adding more to this post, here’s some things I personally think could be changed.  Switch the quarantine building and our character’s quarters (no seriously, why is it so big and bright… I get it, we’re a “commander” or something but we do literally every job except command), put a single guard inside, and have 2-4 cots or chairs that the people sent to quarantine are tied to.  Would still make sense why they’re so pissed/scared while there, no one likes being tied up against their will.  If someone was infected, have where there’s a chance they could break free and kill everyone (including the guard, which could make future days more difficult), and have the chance of them breaking free increase as the game continues (wear and tear would make items less durable, and the lack of resources means you’d have to make do with whatever you can).
Speaking of resources, if there’s issues with supply or there’s some sort of corruption/funneling of resources elsewhere, they need to indicate that more.  The survivor area and lack of guards is a good start.  They even mention that the Insta-Zombie Identifier has limited use.  But then we’re given unlimited ammo and can call in an airstrike, and there’s two entire trucks to pick up 5 people?  Cool idea for protecting the camp and convoy, and I can see how the truck selection could be fun once the game is finished, but it also tells me that there is no lack of resources.  Sure, maybe the group in control decided to allocate more resources into killing zombies, in which case there needs to be some sort of indication of that (the guards or civilians gossiping, an email or note from whoever was in charge before you, etc).  Maybe this whole camp is actually supposed to act like bait for a giant trap, that would be a fun idea.  As for protecting the camp/convoy, could be changed to where each bullet costs quite a bit or the more bullets/airstrikes you use, the more favors you have to do for higher ups (let this specific person through, kill this person, etc).  You can fill up a truck with 20 people, but there’s only one truck.  At first, very few zombies are wandering around and rarely attack the camp.  But the more active the camp is (more people, more generators used, the more often you use an airstrike, etc), the more zombies there are wandering around the camp and actively attacking.  If you fill up the truck(s) too much, more zombies will try to attack the convoy (also if the trucks are indestructible to an airstrike, then I’m sure they can tank a couple of zombies).  The bait you can use (that didn’t really… work) would make much more sense then.  The idea of using a drone is cool too, but just have it be a guy on the wall when the camp is attacked and someone in the truck during the escort.  Does the exact same thing but with more limitations and I don’t have to keep wondering where the energy to charge a drone is coming from.
I could keep going, there’s many things that could be done to make the game more believable (as much as it can be for a zombie apocalypse game) while still making it fun or difficult.  And that’s not to say that the game doesn’t have good stuff, I really like the idea of doing a medical examination on these people, learning more and more about symptoms of this virus, having to weigh the risks of someone turning into a zombie versus them just being sick.  I would love to play it once it’s fully released, though I hope that the dev makes some changes.
TLDR I know what game mechanics and resources are, and there’s some stuff that could be changed in the game that would make it more enjoyable/immersive.  I just didn’t think anyone would breeze past “I get *why*” and then decide to comment about how I clearly don’t understand how games or the real world works.  Silly me!
(For those of you being respectful while stating your opinions/thoughts about the “why,” I appreciate you and that last bit was not aimed at you ❤)
